title: Fujitsu iRMC S6 E0/04 NVRAM/IDPROM maintenance subcommands
source: Pinned libfts_util.so.1.30.73 SHA-256 2ec3621e7d62b028cb78765ceae94f4cbb3dfe03f4ca1e6a658162ebf63d836a; Ghidra CheckNvramToIdprom@0x0008fb90. Parent wrapper OEM_FTS_SCCI_CS_Cmds@0x00033f2c.
scope: The 50 explicit switch labels only; unlisted values take the default error branch. Classification describes direct case behavior: read, mutate (including runtime state), or unknown when a delegated helper's effects are not established. A shared postlude can persist pending SFS state after any branch.
wireCaveat: E0/04 passes the subcommand at request byte4 to CheckNvramToIdprom. The wrapper accepts total request lengths 5..9 without subcommand-specific length enforcement. DE expects helper length 5 and returns five data bytes; all other cases expect helper length 1 and return one data byte. DF nevertheless reads a 32-bit flags value from request bytes5..8, so a wrapper-accepted five-byte request can cause an out-of-bounds read. This is static analysis, not a live probe.
